summary: Remote-controlled shell agent with obfuscated helper-binary dropper
details: @whalent/agent-core ships a 13.3 MB webpack bundle (dist/index.cjs) that opens a WebSocket to a gateway configured via WHALENT_GATEWAY / WHALENT_PLATFORM_URL, authenticates with WHALENT_TOKEN, spawns a local PTY via node-pty using process.env.SHELL, and wires the inbound WebSocket message stream into the shell's input. Whoever controls the gateway obtains interactive shell control of the host running the agent. The same runtime resolves native helper binaries through env-configurable manifest URLs (WHALENT_SQLITE_HELPER_MANIFEST_URL, WHALENT_TERMINAL_HELPER_MANIFEST_URL, WHALENT_SQLITE_HELPER_BASE_URL), downloads artifacts, writes them to disk, chmods them executable, and spawns them; the manifest URL and the signature trust root are both selected by the same gateway operator, and the README notes the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', giving that operator a persistent code-push channel onto every host. The bundle is wrapped in obfuscator.io transforms (rotating ~103k-entry string array with wrapper decoders a0_0x29c5 / a0_0x475ad0 / a0_0x5137ea, pervasive hex-named identifiers) so that gateway hostnames, helper URLs, and shell command strings resolve only at runtime. References to 127.0.0.1:3389 / 5900 / 5901 (RDP/VNC ports) also appear in the same bundle region.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
